test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: maths
question: A lady sold an article for Rs. 960 at some profit. Had she sold it for Rs. 800, then there would have been a loss equal to (1)/(3) of the initial profit. What was the profit percentage of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between two selling prices = 960 − 800 = 160.

Ratio of Profit to Loss = 3 : 1 (since Loss = 1/3 Profit).

Total ratio units (3 + 1) = 4 units → 160.

1 unit (Loss) = 40 | 3 units (Profit) = 120.

Cost Price (CP) = 960 − 120 = 840.

Profit % = (120 ÷ 840) × 100 = 100/7%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First selling price (SP₁) = ₹960

Second selling price (SP₂) = ₹800

Condition: Loss = 1/3 × Profit

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Loss = CP − SP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35762d6a5fd856882f4444729ac37d1db0d7d16c27f03297c1da3169b57acfbe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial Profit = P

⇒ Loss = P/3

⇒ CP = 960 − P (From scenario 1)

⇒ CP = 800 + P/3 (From scenario 2)

⇒ 960 − P = 800 + P/3

⇒ 960 − 800 = P + P/3

⇒ 160 = 4P/3

⇒ P = (160 × 3) ÷ 4

⇒ P = 120

⇒ CP = 960 − 120 = ₹840

⇒ Profit % = (120 ÷ 840) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1/7) × 100 = 100/7%

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Marked Price (MP) is the price listed on the label. Discount is always calculated on MP: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount = (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Formula

Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100, where error is the weight difference.
